passage: I'm Naveen. In our mock round, the quiz master began, "Which river flows through..." and I slammed the buzzer before the sentence ended. "The Ganga!" "Wrong," said Chaitanya, our quiz master. "The question was, which river flows through Hyderabad, in the south." Everyone laughed. I lost five points. I did it again, and again. Each time I heard only the first four or five words and was sure I knew. My team's score sank. I felt hot in the face, and my fingers itched to press anyway. The quiz master waited every time for the question to end, and I never did.

qa.q: Which river did Naveen wrongly answer?
What was Naveen feeling after the wrong answers?
qa.a: Naveen felt embarrassed and impatient, shown by the hot face and fingers itching to press anyway.

qa.a: Naveen could count silently to two after the quiz master stops, or listen to the whole question before pressing. That extra moment would catch the change at the end.

qa.a: Chaitanya waited for each question to end while Naveen jumped in early, so Chaitanya probably sees an eager player who needs to listen longer.

Quiz coach's note, mock round, Thursday
Varun is one of our quickest boys, and he loves the buzzer. Today he pressed it on five questions before I had finished reading them. "Which planet is closest to the sun, and which" - buzz - "Mercury!" The question was about the planet with the most moons. He got four of those five wrong and lost twenty points. He was frustrated and said the questions were tricky. I explained that quiz questions often turn at the end. We practised a rule: wait until the question mark, count one, then buzz. In the last ten questions he waited, got three right, and made no mistakes. I will keep reminding him.
- Lalit

qa.q: How many points did Varun lose on the early buzzes?
How did Varun feel after losing the points?
qa.a: He felt frustrated and blamed the questions for being tricky.

qa.q: What other approach might suit Varun's quickness, and why?
qa.a: He could listen for the key word at the end of each question before buzzing, because his speed is useful only when he knows what is being asked.

qa.q: How do Varun's early buzzes look to Lalit?
qa.a: Lalit sees a quick boy losing points he doesn't need to lose, and patiently helps him with a simple rule.

grounding: It shows a boy buzzing as soon as he hears the first words, often getting it wrong because the question changes at the end, and losing points.

Wednesday
Diary, today's practice quiz was terrible. I was SO fast. I buzzed before anyone. But Darshan sir kept saying "Wrong" and taking away points. One question started "Who wrote the national anthem" and I buzzed and said the name, but the question went on, "and in which language?" Which was the part they wanted. Three times that happened. Our team ended with minus ten, and Darshan sir said I was answering questions nobody had asked yet. Everyone laughed. I laughed too, but I felt stupid. Tomorrow I'm going to sit on my buzzer hand until the question ends. Really.
- Omkar
